title: The Hitopadesha
author: Narayana (trad.)
translator: Sir Edwin Arnold, The Book of Good Counsels (public domain, Project Gutenberg #13268)
blurb: 'Beneficial advice': Sanskrit fables of crows, deer, tigers and kings, packed with verses on friendship, money and war.

enmity.e: The old enmity between the families ended at the wedding.

scripture.e: She quoted scripture at the ceremony.

scripture-learning.e: She quoted scripture at the ceremony.

fate.m: A force believed to decide events.
fate.e: He blamed fate for the missed train.

cards.title: An unlikely friendship
cards.text: A crow asks a mouse to be his friend. The mouse laughs — crows eat mice! The story asks whether trust can cross natural enmity.
cards.qLife: Making friends with a rival team's player.
cards.cap: The lion, crow, wolf and jackal, Kalila wa Dimna · public domain

cards.title: Money and respect
cards.text: A bitter verse: people treat wealth as friends, family and even wisdom — and the fable calls this a shame.
cards.quote: Wealth is friends, home, father, brother
cards.qMean: Money buys people's attention and respect.
cards.qLife: Suddenly having many 'friends' after a lottery win.
cards.cap: The merchant returns, Tuti-nama, Mughal, 16th century · public domain

cards.title: Some things never change
cards.text: However learned a cheat is, he's still a cheat; however bitter the pasture, a cow's milk is sweet. Nature shows through.
cards.quote: Be his Scripture-learning wondrous, yet the cheat will be a cheat
cards.qMean: Education doesn't change a dishonest nature.
cards.qLife: A well-spoken scammer is still a scammer.

cards.title: Lions must hunt
cards.text: Fate isn't enough: even a hungry lion must hunt, for no deer walks into his den while he sleeps.
cards.quote: While the hungry lion slumbers, not a deer comes to his den.
cards.qMean: Success needs effort; it won't come to you while you sleep.
cards.qLife: Job offers don't arrive unless you apply.
cards.cap: Abu'l Hasan, Raja Anup Rai intercepting a lion, c. 1615 · public domain
